analysis: The broad option combines sociology, politics and psychology with empirical methods. Applied work in water governance, sustainability, public policy, inclusion and youth resilience supplies distinct societal applications. Living with Water studies delta communities in place but does not supply UvA’s urban social geography sequence.

The inequality option gives sustained weight to legal institutions, rights, gender history and redistribution, with sociology, policy and political research linking the fields. EU law, constitutional rights and historical evidence distinguish this from the broad behavioural option.

The health option applies public health, health psychology, econometrics, evidence synthesis and public policy to inequality, determinants and services. Removing a biomedical gateway and Infection & Immunity leaves the defining social and behavioural focus, and adds prediction assessment and policy research. The dedicated UvA health modules corroborate this direction.

Three substantively distinct options pass the published feasibility and distinctness gates. No fourth option is assessed beyond the three-option maximum. Dedicated anthropology and urban social geography remain visible gaps. The 30 EC choice space and 12 EC thesis are not assigned substitutes.

academicConstruction: The economics gateway moves to its available first term in each option, swapping with comparative politics. Public Policy Analysis addresses policy formation and evaluation more directly than international relations. Living with Water makes the broad option more attentive to place and local institutions. The health option adds data modelling and public policy in place of two biomedical units. There are 6, 6 and 11 courses different each way between the three pairs. Alignments address actual methods and topics, including policy stages, conflict and gender, and systematic literature synthesis. Media and general civil-society work remain unmatched to the dedicated practica.
